data.body:
RESEARCH / DECISION BRIEF — read-only evidence collected 2026-08-16 UTC

Measurement method and reproducibility
- Static graph: `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:24,41-44,46-432`, `_build-and-test.yml:43-46,209-236,287-306`, `_mutation.yml:30-90`, and `_optionality.yml:45-48,124-134` at origin/main `b5becd589773602602007a43e84a005fac0310fd`.
- Burst selection: paginated `GET /repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&created=<window>&per_page=100`, grouped into fixed five-minute UTC buckets. The incident-period sample is the largest bucket across all 257 Verified runs on 2026-08-12..13. The current-shape sample is the largest bucket on 2026-08-15..16.
- Job evidence: `GET /repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/<run_id>/jobs?per_page=100`. Queue depth is an event sweep over runner-backed jobs: +1 at job `created_at`, -1/+1 at `started_at`, and -1 at `completed_at`. In the current graph the 13 full-route jobs are created together only after `classify` completes, so `created_at` is an observable runnable-time proxy.
- Gerrit correlation: authenticated read-only `GET /a/changes/?q=comment:<run_id>&o=MESSAGES`; the vote comments map every cited run to an exact Gerrit change. No GitHub, Gerrit, Jira, or workflow state was changed.

Current per-run slot cost
- Docs-only route: 5 runner jobs: clear, require-ticket, classify, docs-only, vote.
- Full route with no mutation shard: 17 runner jobs. Formula: three serial admission jobs + 13 full-route jobs + vote. The 13-way fan-out is build lint/pip-audit/4 pytest cells (6), mutation selector (1), optionality (2), artifact probe (1), eval discipline (1), golden path (1), and verify identity (1).
- Full route with N selected mutation shards: `17 + N`, where `0 <= N <= 7`; maximum 24 runner jobs. Peak theoretical runnable demand is 13 immediately after classification and `12 + N` after the selector, maximum 19. There is exactly one macOS job per full run.
- Live confirmations: run 31900256967 executed 17 runner jobs / 3,935 runner-seconds (65.6 runner-minutes), no mutation shards. Run 31900214367 executed 24 runner jobs / 6,997 runner-seconds (116.6 runner-minutes), all seven shards. Its macOS cell occupied 1,425 seconds (23m45s).

Observed burst depth
1. Incident-period peak, 2026-08-13 20:30 UTC: seven runs in five minutes: 31741187649, 31741458352, 31741476017, 31741500566, 31741503429, 31741506784, 31741510115. Gerrit maps these to five distinct changes (1736, 1737, 1738, 1742, 1743), including two replacement dispatches. Across runner-backed jobs the sample reached 22 waiting jobs at 20:47:30Z and 16 running jobs at 20:56:41Z. Longest observed runner wait was 873s (14m33s) in run 31741506784; another macOS job waited 806s. The seven runs consumed 22,763 runner-seconds (379.4 runner-minutes), including 1,086 seconds in three canceled runs. This is historical workflow shape at trusted-main SHA cecc72b27f.
2. Current-shape peak, 2026-08-15 17:30 UTC: three independent full-route runs in five minutes, Gerrit 1813/run 31898545665, 1814/run 31898595256, and 1815/run 31898602868. Each executed 17 jobs with no mutation shards. At 17:35:03Z, run 1813 had 7 jobs running, run 1814 had all 13 full-route jobs waiting, and run 1815 had 4 running plus 9 waiting: 22 waiting jobs inside this repository alone. Maximum running was 15. Longest wait was 197s (3m17s), job 95045898392, Ubuntu/Python 3.11 in run 31898595256. The three runs consumed 11,846 runner-seconds (197.4 runner-minutes).

Capacity evidence and limits
- `GET /orgs/navapbc` on 2026-08-16 reports `plan.name=free` (and 618 filled seats).
- GitHub public limits documentation, https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits, reports Standard GitHub-hosted runner limits: Free 20 total / 5 macOS; Pro 40 / 5; Team 60 / 5; Enterprise 500 / 50. The table states these are plan-level concurrency limits and the macOS limit is shared.
- The Actions API has no historical organization-wide job timeline available to this credential. Therefore 22 waiting is a repository-local lower bound, not the full navapbc queue. The current burst had only 15 of this repositorys jobs running at peak despite more being runnable; that is consistent with shared-org contention, but the split between other repositories, runner provisioning delay, and label-specific availability is not directly observable. The billing endpoint was also unavailable to this credential (HTTP 404 / missing admin:org), so no spend claim is made.

Four mutually exclusive FIRST-MOVE options (remeasure before combining)

A. COVERAGE-NEUTRAL DEMAND REDUCTION — RECOMMENDED
Bundle the four short always-on Ubuntu preflights (artifact probe, eval discipline, golden path, verify identity) into one isolated sequential preflight job, and cap the mutation matrix at `max-parallel: 3`. Every command, assertion, OS/Python cell, and selected mutation shard still runs; only scheduling changes.
- Slots: full no-mutation `17 -> 14`; maximum-shard `24 -> 21`. Immediate fan-out `13 -> 10`; upper simultaneous demand `19 -> 12` (the preflight saves 3 and the mutation cap saves up to 4). Three simultaneous base full routes request 30 rather than 39 immediate jobs.
- Latency model from run 31900214367: the four preflights consumed 210 aggregate runner-seconds and 82s parallel wall; sequential worst case adds about 128s to that branch, still far below the macOS critical path. With the seven measured shard durations and manifest order, three mutation lanes finish in about 21m15s after selection versus about 14m35s today, still below that runs 23m47s remaining macOS path. Expected sample wall impact: approximately zero; faster-mac or mutation-heavy changes could wait several minutes.
- Risks: environment contamination, loss of independent failure diagnostics, or a first failure skipping later checks. The implementation plan must use isolated venv/worktree boundaries and an all-checks-run result accumulator, preserving the prior optionality-collapse precedent.
- Exact repository scope: `gerrit-verify.yaml`, `_mutation.yml`, extraction seams used by `_artifact-probe.yml`, `_eval-discipline.yml`, `test.yml`, and `verify-identity.yml`, plus workflow parity/policy tests (`tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py`, `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py`, `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py`). No implementation until this CI behavior is approved and separately plan-reviewed.

B. COALESCE SUPERSEDED PATCHSETS BEFORE DISPATCH
The current workflow already groups by Gerrit Change-Id and cancels in progress (`gerrit-verify.yaml:41-44`). Merged fix 4cbaa19315 also made every full-route predicate cancellation-aware. Organic pairs prove the residual: run 31846910968 -> 31847788055 delayed successor admission 78s and consumed 127 post-replacement runner-seconds; 31847788055 -> 31849555779 delayed 110s and consumed 107 seconds.
- Effect ceiling: save about 1.8-2.1 runner-minutes and 78-110s per actual supersession. It does nothing for independent-change bursts, the dominant current sample.
- A short debounce would not have coalesced the observed pairs: replacements arrived about 13m34s and 28m28s after their predecessors. A debounce long enough to do so adds that delay to every patchset. Cross-change coalescing is invalid because each change requires its own Verified vote.
- Risks: stale or missing votes, delayed feedback, and stateful dispatcher recovery. Exact scope requires a gerrit-to-platform capability/fork, then `infra/compose/Dockerfile.gerrit`, `infra/gerrit/gerrit_to_platform.ini.template`, materialization/config checks, and the two-vote runbook. Recommendation: do not choose; the high-value cancellation behavior already exists.

C. MOVE macOS FROM PRE-MERGE VERIFIED TO SIX-HOURLY MAIN HEALTH
Keep the macOS/Python 3.13 cell in the shared scheduled branch-health workflow but exclude it when `_build-and-test.yml` receives Gerrit coordinates.
- Slots: full route `17+N -> 16+N`; total peak `19 -> 18`, but the scarce macOS demand becomes zero pre-merge instead of one of the Free plans five macOS slots for roughly 20-30 minutes per full run.
- Latency from current evidence: run 31900214367 would have been limited by mutation at about 16m41s rather than completing in 25m53s, an estimated 9m12s saving. No-mutation run 31900256967 would have been limited by Ubuntu at about 14m47s rather than 26m14s, about 11m27s saved.
- Risk: macOS-specific flock/mkdir/gtimeout/platform regressions can merge and are detected only by the next scheduled main-health run, up to roughly six hours later. This is a real pre-merge coverage-policy change.
- Exact scope: `_build-and-test.yml`, `gerrit-verify.yaml`, `test.yml`, workflow parity/policy tests, and CI contributor documentation.

D. BUY CAPACITY: UPGRADE THE ORGANIZATION PLAN
Move navapbc from Free to Team. The public limit rises from 20 to 60 total concurrent standard jobs, enough for the observed three-run 39-job immediate fan-out and the 24-job maximum single run.
- Slots/latency: no workflow slot reduction; the current repository-local queue should largely disappear until wider org demand reaches 60. The macOS limit remains 5, so a burst of six full Verifies can still queue macOS.
- Risks/cost: organization-wide recurring billing/governance impact. The API reports 618 filled seats; pricing and eligible-seat scope require an organization administrator and were not inferred here.
- Exact scope: GitHub organization billing/plan administration only; no repository files. Remeasure the same run/job metrics after any change.

Recommendation
Choose Option A as the first intervention. It addresses independent-change bursts, retains all pre-merge coverage, avoids recurring organization spend, and has a concrete bounded effect on both base and worst-case fan-out. Option B has low incremental value after 4cbaa19315. Option C has the largest macOS latency benefit but deliberately weakens pre-merge behavior. Option D is operationally simple but costly and leaves the five-job macOS ceiling intact.

Ticket state
Research acceptance is satisfied. No remediation was selected or implemented by the investigator. Keep this ticket in_progress pending the operator decision; after approval, rewrite the chosen implementation plan, run `rebar review-plan`, and dispatch under the required held-out TDD workflow.
